# `Browser.Permission.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Permission.Internals — the low-level Permissions API port
surface: the closed outbound/inbound ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js`
request/subscribe wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.Permission` layer wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:permission` axis as the
top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the `Ipe.Browser.Permission` path
prefix), so the raw port surface cannot be reached undisclosed.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type.

  * `Query name` — one-shot: query the current state of a single permission.
  * `Watch name` — begin a continuous stream; each state change event
    delivers a fresh reading on the inbound subscription.

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type — NOT the app's internal `Msg`. Every
variant the browser can push is enumerated, so the fold in the high-level
layer is EXHAUSTIVE and a denial becomes a typed `Err`, never a silent drop.

  * `StateGranted` — the permission is currently granted.
  * `StateDenied` — the permission is currently denied; querying it again without a
    user gesture yields the same result.
  * `StatePrompt` — the browser will prompt the user on the next relevant API call.
  * `StateUnavailable` — the Permissions API is absent in this context.

Variants are prefixed with `State` to avoid clashing with the public
`PermissionState` constructors (`Granted`, `Denied`, `Prompt`) in modules
that import both.

## `PermissionName`

The closed set of queryable permission names.

Each constructor maps to its W3C Permissions API name string; only the
Baseline-supported names are covered.

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.
The served first-party JS sink reaches `navigator.permissions.query`; the
reply arrives inbound as a `JsMsg`.

## `requestOne`

```ipe
requestOne : JsCmd -> Task Error JsMsg
```

`requestOne cmd` — correlated one-shot `JsCmd` → `Task Error JsMsg`.
Routes through `Js.request` with the `inbound` decoder so the correlated
reply is decoded fail-closed by the same gate the `subscribe` path uses.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for the inbound `JsMsg`. It reads the `ok`
flag: a true flag decodes a `state` string into the closed state vocabulary;
a false flag decodes the closed `error` vocabulary. An unrecognised token
fails the decode closed (the frame is dropped).
